title: GitHub - DamiMartinez/book-skills: Claude Code skills, one per book. Each triggers automatically when you mention that book's concepts, not just its title.
excerpt: Claude Code skills, one per book. Each triggers automatically when you mention that book's concepts, not just its title. - DamiMartinez/book-skills
content_html:
A collection of Claude Code skills, one per book. Each skill packages a book's core framework so Claude applies it automatically whenever you mention the book's ideas — not just when you say the book's title.

Example: with the lean-startup skill installed, asking Claude to "help me plan this new feature, I want a lean approach" or "how do I validate this before building it" will make Claude structure its answer around Build-Measure-Learn, MVPs, and actionable metrics — no need to say "use the lean startup skill."

Available skills

Skill Book Topic
lean-startup The Lean Startup — Eric Ries Product/startup validation: MVP, Build-Measure-Learn, validated learning, pivot vs. persevere
high-output-management High Output Management — Andrew S. Grove Management: managerial leverage, task-relevant maturity, one-on-ones, indicators, decision-making
hard-thing-about-hard-things The Hard Thing About Hard Things — Ben Horowitz Leadership under pressure: wartime/peacetime CEO, no-easy-answers decisions, firing/layoffs, Law of Crappy People
pragmatic-programmer The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th Anniversary Ed. — Hunt & Thomas Engineering practice: DRY, orthogonality, coupling, Design by Contract, refactoring, requirements, automation
ai-modern-approach Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach — Russell & Norvig AI/algorithm design: PEAS, agent architectures, search (uninformed/A*/minimax), CSPs, Bayesian networks, MDPs
machine-learning-mitchell Machine Learning — Tom M. Mitchell ML fundamentals: T/P/E framing, bias-variance, evaluation methodology, MAP/naive Bayes, PAC learning, algorithm selection
c-programming-language The C Programming Language, 2nd Ed. — Kernighan & Ritchie C code: pointer arithmetic, declaration reading, manual memory ownership, undefined behavior, preprocessor/linkage
automate-boring-stuff Automate the Boring Stuff with Python — Al Sweigart Task automation: file ops, CSV/Excel/PDF handling, web scraping, scheduling, safe-automation habits

More skills (product management, programming languages, design patterns, system architecture, data engineering, etc.) get added over time — see Contributing.

Installation

Skills are plain folders with a SKILL.md file. Claude Code discovers them from a skills/ directory — either globally (available in every project) or per-project (available only in that repo).

1. Clone this repo:

git clone https://github.com/DamiMartinez/book-skills.git

2. Install a skill — pick one:

  • Global (recommended) — available in every Claude Code session on your machine:

    ln -s "$(pwd)/book-skills/skills/lean-startup" ~/.claude/skills/lean-startup

  • Per-project — available only inside one project:

    mkdir -p /path/to/your-project/.claude/skills
ln -s "$(pwd)/book-skills/skills/lean-startup" /path/to/your-project/.claude/skills/lean-startup

    (Symlinking keeps the skill up to date when you git pull this repo. Copying the folder instead works too, it just won't auto-update.)

3. Repeat step 2 for each skill you want, or install all of them at once:

for skill in book-skills/skills/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$skill")
  [ "$name" = "_template" ] && continue
  ln -s "$(pwd)/$skill" ~/.claude/skills/"$name"
done

No restart needed — Claude Code picks up skills at the start of a session.

How triggering works

Claude Code decides whether to use a skill based on its description field, matched against what you're asking. You don't need to name the book or the skill — mentioning the book's concepts (e.g. "validated learning," "MVP," "build-measure-learn") is enough. Skills only kick in for tasks substantial enough to benefit from them; simple one-off questions may not trigger one even if related.

Contributing

Adding a skill for a new book:

  1. Copy the template: cp -r skills/_template skills/<book-slug>
  2. Fill in SKILL.md:
    • description — list the book's key terms explicitly (not just the title); this is what makes the skill trigger correctly
    • Core concepts — 3-8 ideas actually worth applying, not a full book summary
    • How to apply this — concrete steps for how Claude should structure its response when the skill fires
  3. Test it in a real conversation and tune the description if it doesn't trigger as expected
  4. Update the table above and open a PR

Keep each skill focused on what's actionable from the book, not exhaustive coverage of it.

License

MIT

安装

技能是带有 SKILL.md 文件的普通文件夹。 Claude Code 从技能/目录中发现它们 - 全局（在每个项目中可用）或每个项目（仅在该存储库中可用）。

1. 克隆这个仓库：

git clone https://github.com/DamiMartinez/book-skills.git

2. 安装一项技能 - 选择一个：

  • 全局（推荐）— 在您计算机上的每个 Claude Code 会话中可用： ln -s "$(pwd)/book-skills/skills/lean-startup" ~/.claude/skills/lean-startup
  • 每个项目 - 仅在一个项目内可用： mkdir -p /path/to/your-project/.claude/skills ln -s "$(pwd)/book-skills/skills/lean-startup" /path/to/your-project/.claude/skills/lean-startup （当您 git pull 此存储库时，符号链接使技能保持最新状态。 复制文件夹也可以，只是不会自动更新。）

3. 对您想要的每项技能重复步骤 2，或一次安装所有技能：

for skill in book-skills/skills/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$skill")
  [ "$name" = "_template" ] && continue
  ln -s "$(pwd)/$skill" ~/.claude/skills/"$name"
done

无需重新启动 - 克劳德·科德 (Claude Code) 在课程开始时即可掌握技能。

触发如何工作

Claude Code 根据技能的描述字段决定是否使用技能，并与您的要求相匹配。 您不需要命名这本书或技能 - 提及这本书的概念（例如“验证学习”、“MVP”、“构建-测量-学习”）就足够了。 技能只有在完成足以从中受益的实质性任务时才会发挥作用；简单的一次性问题即使相关，也可能不会触发问题。

贡献

为新书添加技能：

  1. 复制模板：cp -r Skills/_template Skills/<book-slug>
  2. 填写SKILL.md：描述——明确列出本书的关键术语（不仅仅是标题）；这就是使技能正确触发的原因 核心概念 - 3-8 个实际上值得应用的想法，而不是完整的书籍摘要 如何应用 - 当技能触发时克劳德应如何构建其响应的具体步骤
  3. 在真实对话中进行测试，如果未按预期触发，则调整描述
  4. 更新上表并打开 PR

让每项技能都集中在书中可操作的内容上，而不是详尽地涵盖它。
